title: Step 64-B backend/OpenAPI Customer Account & After-Sales contract readiness
description: High-risk Stage B for Step 64. Audit and repair evidence-backed Account/Auth, Orders/After-Sales and customer in-app notification HTTP contract gaps before Storefront Account implementation. Preserve backend business authority; do not invent legacy design-only customer tools.

dependencies.evidence: PR #316 merged; exact-SHA Canonical CI #1353 and Phase A #852 PASS; terminal Lock release comment 5981015509.

audit_findings: Auth session/logout/logout-all success bodies are untyped; logout routes advertise stale 202.
Returns customer create/list/detail/cancel contracts are generic or stale; runtime create/cancel are idempotency-protected and create defaults to 201.
Returns customer timeline lacks complete customer-session/path/error contract.
Warranty customer create/list/detail contracts are generic; runtime create is idempotency-protected and defaults to 201.
Warranty customer timeline lacks complete customer-session/path/error contract.
NotificationInAppService exists with owner-scoped list/markRead/acknowledge but no customer-facing HTTP controller route exists.
Legacy OpenAPI customer Product Alerts/Loyalty/Review operations have no matching customer-facing runtime controller discovered; Step 64 treats them as NO_ACTION, not executable authority.

acceptance_criteria.description: Auth session/logout/logout-all contract matches runtime response bodies and actual statuses without exposing session secrets.
Customer Returns create/list/detail/timeline/cancel contracts match runtime ownership, typed success, status and idempotency semantics.
Customer Warranty create/list/detail/timeline contracts match runtime ownership, typed success, status and idempotency semantics.
Customer in-app notification list/read/acknowledge HTTP routes are customer-only wrappers over existing owner-scoped NotificationInAppService and do not add database/provider/business-rule scope.
Legacy Product Alert/Loyalty/Review OpenAPI-only operations are not consumed by Step 64 Storefront unless runtime authority is separately proven.
Generated TypeScript is byte-for-byte reproducible from canonical OpenAPI; focused tests and canonical verify pass.
No DB migration, dependency change, Wholesale, Storefront C+ implementation or new after-sales eligibility rule is introduced.

HIGH-risk terminal closure requires exact-head Canonical CI, Phase A, deterministic Review, Security PASS, exact-artifact HUMAN approval and Lock, merge, exact-SHA postmerge and terminal Lock release.

external_gate_evidence.rule: Step 64-B is HIGH risk. Final HUMAN approval must bind to the frozen exact head and artifact after technical/security gates pass. Direct-main mutation is prohibited.
